rubric_items.reason: API, web and db modules, both endpoints and the patient table are listed with correct change status; the existing dashboard test that asserts the exact totals shape is not listed.
Every module, API and table id exists in the generated facts and each is cited; claims point at fact ids or exact source lines that hold the quoted text.
Callers via client.ts, jobs and the /patients UI route are covered, but the dashboard test reading totals with toEqual and the patients page's lack of a visible period filter are missed.
Statuses rest on facts and on req.md decisions; the no-call-edges limit is stated. The REQ-10 reading versus split S-3 AC5 is settled as known without a cited basis for the split story.
Readable and well structured with a clear summary and default; impacted items are listed by module rather than ordered by risk.

findings.text: Adding a New patients count to the dashboard totals breaks the existing API test that asserts the totals object with toEqual; the artifact says the existing totals stay as they are but does not list this reader.

cites.quote: Its response gains a New patients count; the existing totals stay as they are (C5).

findings.suggested_fix: List api/test/dashboard.test.ts (DSH-1..6 totals toEqual) as an indirect effect that must be updated, or place the new count outside totals.

findings.text: PatientsPage builds its filters from q, status and page only and has no control for a registration period, so a period carried in the URL would be invisible to staff and could not be cleared; the artifact notes only passing it to the API.

cites.quote: const filters = { q: params.get('q') ?? '', status: params.get('status') ?? '', page: params.get('page') ?? '1' };
the patients page must pass the new filter from the URL to the API (C13)

findings.suggested_fix: Add an indirect effect: the patients page needs a visible, clearable indicator of the registration-period filter.

findings.text: The artifact tells design to test the fixed list order instead of split story S-3 AC5, but cites neither the split story nor records the mismatch as a cross-step item; S-3 AC5 still requires a user-chosen sort the code lacks.

cites.quote: Story S-3 AC5 in the split step assumes a user-chosen sort order, which the code does not offer.
Given staff chose a sort order on the patient list other than its default

findings.suggested_fix: Cite split.md#item:S-3 and the fixed ORDER BY line, and record the S-3 AC5 mismatch so design rewrites that AC explicitly.

cites.quote: Counts only: no contact details or medical history (DSH-9).
ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC
CREATE INDEX patient_created_idx ON patient (created_at DESC, id DESC);
The web app talks to the API only through `web/src/api/client.ts`.
The tile shows the number of patients whose `created_at` falls in the selected period.
